label: early copy step (recall 2-3) in long sequences, input digit 3
explanation: Very sparse and weak unit (max activation 0.012, about 0.03% of steps). Fires only in the copy phase, never on original or delimiter steps, and almost only early in the copy: recall_idx 2 holds 67% of the mass and recall_idx 3 holds 25%. It is concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 84% of the mass, L=8 16%, nothing at L<=6). The strongest token cue is the input being the digit 3 (the fed-back original token 1), which holds 60% of the mass; inputs 1 and d come next. Rate rises with how many digits the sequence contains. The top activations are all input 3 at recall_idx 2 in L=9 sequences, often with repeated 3s. Position alone (copy, recall 2-3, L>=8) covers 89% of activations but has precision of only 0.5%. Adding input==3 brings precision to about 12-19% and recall to 27-35%, so most steps matching the predicate stay below threshold and many activations fall on other tokens. This looks like a weak, near-threshold response to a digit input at an early copy position, not a clean detector.
